name: Semantic Topic Consistency
description: Measures the degree of 'topic drift' or semantic variance throughout a document. Human cognition is naturally associative; when writing a long text, human authors organically drift through related sub-topics, tangent thoughts, or personal anecdotes, causing the semantic focus to evolve continuously. In contrast, generative AI models are mathematically anchored to their initial prompt via attention mechanisms. Consequently, they maintain an artificially tight, laser-focused consistency on the core topic from the first sentence to the last, rarely exhibiting the natural, messy semantic wandering characteristic of human thought.
mechanism: The algorithm segments the text into continuous blocks using a sliding window approach. It generates dense vector embeddings (e.g., via BERT or similar transformer encoders) for each segment. It then calculates the cosine similarity sequence between adjacent segments, as well as the similarity of every segment back to the opening thesis. A text that maintains an extraordinarily high and uniform cosine similarity across all segments (near-zero semantic drift) strongly indicates algorithmic generation constrained by a rigid attention window.
useCase: Highly effective for analyzing long-form content, such as essays, articles, or multi-page reports, where natural human topic drift should theoretically be most apparent.
strengths:
• Language-agnostic approach, as it relies on fundamental semantic vector representations rather than syntax or grammar rules.
• Excellent at catching AI text that has been deliberately generated to look long and comprehensive, as the AI will inadvertently expose its lack of natural topic evolution.
limitations:
• Ineffective on very short texts (under 200 words) where neither humans nor AI have the space to exhibit topic drift.
• Can produce false positives on highly rigid human academic papers, technical manuals, or structured legal documents which demand absolute, unwavering topical focus.
parameters:
Analysis: Vector Embedding Similarity Mapping
Metric: Inter-Segment Cosine Similarity & Global Semantic Variance
Output: 0-100 Artificial Topic Rigidity Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 75-85% on long-form text. Extremely powerful when correlated with structural predictability metrics.

references.title: Bakhtin, A. et al. (2019). Real or Fake? Learning to Discriminate Machine from Human Text. NeurIPS.
Zellers, R. et al. (2019). Defending Against Neural Fake News. NeurIPS.
